value: Cohort size: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive, 99 hypertensive; total 196 Chinese individuals
Source: Kailuan Group Corporation, Tangshan, northern China
Study design: cross-sectional metagenomic and metabolomic analysis with fecal microbiota transplantation
Fecal microbiota transplanted from 3 donors (2 HTN, 1 control) to germ-free mice
BP measured by tail-cuff method in mice at 10 weeks post-transplantation
Total sequencing: 1211 Gb, 125-bp paired-end reads; average 6.18±1.43 million reads per sample
HTN mice showed significantly higher SBP, DBP, MBP vs controls: P=0.018, P=0.019, P=0.014 respectively
Disease classifier AUC for control vs HTN: 0.91 (95% CI 0.75-1); control vs pHTN: 0.89 (95% CI 0.65-1)
Metabolomic subset: 30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN; n=124 total
All HTN subjects were newly diagnosed, prior to antihypertensive treatment

uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional metadata documenting study design, sample sizes, analytical methods, and key findings.

host_species.evidence_quote: cohort of 196 Chinese individuals; fecal samples from donors
host_species.notes: Primary study population is human; fecal transplantation experiments also conducted in Mus musculus (germ-free mice).

extraction_warnings: Study reports cohort-level summary data only; individual subject IDs and sample IDs not provided
Paper does not provide age values for individual participants; only notes no remarkable regularity of bacterial abundance based on age
No NCBI/ENA accessions provided for raw sequencing data
Sequencing platform specified as 'Illumina' but exact model (HiSeq/MiSeq/etc.) inferred from read length and dataset size
Gender ratio mentioned as discrepant but individual sex assignments not reported
Granularity is study_level because paper presents aggregated data by group, not individual sample records
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('study_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension', 'Hypertension', 'HTN mice (FMT recipients)', 'Control mice (FMT recipients)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Human participant ages in years not reported in provided paper sections.
Gender distribution noted as discrepant among groups but specific values not clearly stated in provided sections.
FMT donor and recipient sample sizes are small (n=3 donors, n=15 recipient mice total).
Pre-hypertensive individuals not included in FMT experiment.
The paper does not report overall survival, ECOG performance status, or tumor measurements; these fields are not applicable to a hypertension/microbiome study.
Specific quantitative biomarker values vary considerably; the paper reports relative abundances, p-values, and directional changes rather than absolute concentrations for most biomarkers.
Germ-free mouse experiments use Mus musculus as host species, distinct from the primary human cohort.
The metabolomic analysis subset (n=124) differs from the full metagenomic cohort (n=196).
BP measurements in mice were obtained at a single timepoint (10 weeks post-transplantation); no longitudinal survival data.
